sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Secondary Sjögren Syndrome (sSS) is defined as the presence of keratoconjunctivitis sicca (KCS) and xerostomia in patients with a pre-existing systemic autoimmune disease, most commonly Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). Unlike Primary Sjögren, sSS occurs later in the disease course and is driven by the underlying connective tissue disease's inflammatory milieu, leading to progressive lymphocytic infiltration and destruction of the lacrimal and salivary glands.

rows: ≤ 5 mm / 5 minutes in at least one eye

sections.title: Comprehensive Ocular Exam Findings
content: Reduced Tear Meniscus Height: < 0.2mm is highly suggestive.
Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT): < 10 seconds (instability); < 5 seconds (severe).
Filamentary Keratitis: Muco-epithelial strands attached to corneal surface.
Mucus Plaquing: Large grey-white opacities in severe KCS.
Lid Margin Disease: Concurrent Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD).
Corneal Neovascularization: Peripheral pannus from chronic inflammation.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Sight-Threatening RA Complications
content: Peripheral Ulcerative Keratitis (PUK): Juxtalimbal thinning/ulceration with epithelial loss.
Necrotizing Scleritis: Severe pain, 'porcelain' white sclera (vasculitis-associated).
Corneal Melting: Sterile 'keratolysis' leading to rapid perforation.
Scleromalacia Perforans: Asymptomatic scleral thinning in long-standing RA.

sections.title: Stepped Management Protocol (TFOS DEWS II)
content: Step 1: Patient education, environmental modification, Preservative-Free (PF) artificial tears, lid hygiene.
Step 2: Punctal plugs, Topical Cyclosporine 0.05% or 0.1%, Lifitegrast 5%, Corticosteroid pulses, Oral secretagogues (Pilocarpine).
Step 3: Oral macrolides (for MGD), Autologous Serum Tears (20% or 50% concentration), Scleral lenses (PROSE).
Step 4: Long-term topical steroids, Amniotic membrane grafting, Surgical punctal occlusion, Tarsorrhaphy.

sections.title: Systemic Investigation Workup
content: Rheumatoid Factor (RF): Elevated in 70-80% of RA.
Anti-Cyclic Citrullinated Peptide (Anti-CCP): More specific than RF (95%).
ANA: Often positive in sSS/RA overlap.
Anti-Ro (SS-A) and Anti-La (SS-B): Hallmarks of Sjögren's.
ESR/CRP: Markers of systemic inflammatory activity.
Salivary Gland Biopsy: If serology is equivocal but clinical suspicion is high.

content.explanation: S: Surface staining (Oxford/SICCA), I: Infiltration (Minor salivary gland biopsy), C: CCP/RF antibodies positive, C: Clinical dry mouth/eye symptoms, A: Anti-SSA/SSB positive.

sections.title: Surgical & Interventional Approaches
content: Punctal Cautery: For definitive occlusion in recalcitrant sSS.
Lateral Tarsorrhaphy: Reduces evaporative surface area in severe exposure/melting.
Amniotic Membrane (ProKera/Cryopreserved): Promotes healing in persistent epithelial defects (PED).
Cyanoacrylate Glue: Emergency management of corneal microperforations in RA melts.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Evidence
sections.content: The TFOS DEWS II (2017) report revolutionized the definition of dry eye to include the role of neurosensory abnormalities. The DREAM Study (2018) questioned the efficacy of Omega-3 fatty acids over placebo for dry eye, highlighting the importance of the tear film's aqueous and lipid components in systemic diseases like RA.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Residents
content: Never treat PUK with topical steroids alone; it usually signals active systemic necrotizing vasculitis and requires urgent systemic immunosuppression.
Secondary Sjögren patients often have more severe ocular surface disease than Primary Sjögren due to the additive effects of RA-related inflammation.
Always check for dental caries and oral health; xerostomia in sSS leads to rapid periodontal decline.
Filamentary keratitis is best treated by manual removal followed by 5% NaCl or topical N-acetylcysteine (10%).
